CHIEF COMPLAINT
Numbness and tingling

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS
The patient is a 60-year-old, right-handed male referred for evaluation of numbness and tingling. He reports symptoms for a few weeks, which started after a car wreck in December when he sustained bilateral wrist fractures. After the wrists healed, he noticed the tingling and numbness more prominently. Symptoms have worsened over the last month. He wears splints on both wrists; the right wrist is worse than the left and the splint provides some relief. He also reports mild stiffness in his neck from hitting his head during the accident, which was diagnosed as a contusion. 

On the right side, symptoms extend from the middle and ring finger up the forearm. On the left side, symptoms extend from the pinky and ring finger. He describes the symptoms as mainly soreness with occasional throbbing and associated weakness, especially with hand use. Tingling occurs more when hands hurt. Symptoms are worse at night and come and go throughout the day. He denies loss of sensation but notes his hands may be less sensitive than normal. He reports being prescribed nerve pain medicine but has not been taking it as directed.

REVIEW OF SYSTEMS
Constitutional: fatigue and weight gain. GI: excessive appetite and bloating. Eyes: floaters. Cardiovascular: shortness of breath and leg swelling. Endocrine: always hungry. Skin: nail bed changes, dryness, and itching. Musculoskeletal: gout and muscle pain. Remainder of systems reviewed and negative.

PAST MEDICAL HISTORY
Car wreck in December with bilateral wrist fractures. Head contusion from motor vehicle accident. Prediabetes, managed with dietary changes. No history of thyroid issues.

MEDICATIONS
Coreg for hypertension. Lexapro for anxiety. Nerve pain medicine (not taking as prescribed).

ALLERGIES
Not discussed.

FAMILY HISTORY
Not discussed.

SOCIAL HISTORY
Right-handed. History of motor vehicle accident in December.

PHYSICAL EXAMINATION
Neurologic examination: Right hand sensation normal except diminished pin prick sensation in third and fourth fingers. Left hand with decreased sensation in fourth and fifth fingers. Reflexes 1+ and symmetric in upper extremities; 2+ in knees; toes downgoing bilaterally. Tinel sign positive at both wrists and both elbows. Rest of exam normal.

RESULTS
Not discussed.

ASSESSMENT AND PLAN
Bilateral carpal tunnel syndrome, though bilateral cubital tunnel syndrome also considered. Plan includes scheduling EMG test to pinpoint the location of nerve irritation. Patient to return for follow-up visit after test results. If symptoms persist, consider referral to hand clinic for injections or carpal tunnel release surgery, or referral to orthopedist for similar treatment. Continue wearing splints.
